 # recorded stream. A compile error, a lathe/sim/motion law or a post-crate
 # unit (lib) test stays P2. An open P2 issue is raised to P1 when a later run
 # fails an output suite; it is never lowered here (a human does that).
+# Order (#3184): each push to main has its own run, so runs can finish out of
+# order. The rolling issue body keeps the last reported commit in a hidden
+# marker (MARK below). A run whose commit is an ancestor of that commit, and
+# not the same commit, reports nothing: an older green run never closes the
+# issue of a newer red run. This needs the full history (fetch-depth: 0).
+# When git cannot decide (an unknown sha), the run reports as before.
 # Provenance: our own AGENTS.md "Issue Law"; GitHub's public gh CLI docs.
 set -uo pipefail
 gh_bin="${GH:-gh}"
@@ -31,13 +37,52 @@ OUTPUT_SUITES='^(golden_cl|solid_law_goldens|recorded_post_streams|recorded_stre
 open=$("$gh_bin" issue list -R "$repo" --state open --label source:agent --search "\"$title\" in:title" \
   --limit 20 --json number,title \
   --jq "[.[] | select(.title == \"$title\")][0].number // empty") || open=""
+# The newest rolling issue, open or closed: it holds the order marker.
+latest=$("$gh_bin" issue list -R "$repo" --state all --label source:agent --search "\"$title\" in:title" \
+  --limit 20 --json number,title \
+  --jq "[.[] | select(.title == \"$title\")][0].number // empty") || latest=""
+[ -n "$latest" ] || latest="$open"
+
+MARK="post-merge-last-sha"
+marker="<!-- $MARK: $sha -->"
+
+# The body of issue $1, or nothing.
+issue_body() { "$gh_bin" issue view "$1" -R "$repo" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+# Write this run's commit into the marker of issue $1. The old marker line is
+# replaced, never kept: the body holds one marker.
+set_marker() {
+  local kept
+  kept=$(issue_body "$1" | sed "/<!-- $MARK: /d")
+  "$gh_bin" issue edit "$1" -R "$repo" --body "$kept
+
+$marker" || exit 1
+}
+
+# Skip a run whose commit is strictly older than the last reported commit.
+if [ -n "$latest" ]; then
+  last=$(issue_body "$latest" | sed -n "s/.*<!-- $MARK: \([0-9a-f]\{7,40\}\) -->.*/\1/p" | tail -n 1)
+  if [ -n "$last" ]; then
+    this_full=$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    last_full=$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$last^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [ -n "$this_full" ] && [ -n "$last_full" ] && [ "$this_full" != "$last_full" ] &&
+      git merge-base --is-ancestor "$this_full" "$last_full" 2>/dev/null; then
+      echo "::notice title=post-merge report skipped::$short is older than the last reported commit ${last:0:10} (#$latest); nothing reported"
+      exit 0
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
 
 if [ "${STATUS:-}" = success ]; then
   if [ -n "$open" ]; then
     "$gh_bin" issue comment "$open" -R "$repo" --body "Green again: the post-merge batch gate passed on \`$sha\` (${RUN_URL:-no run url}). Closing; a new red run opens a new issue." || exit 1
+    set_marker "$open"
     "$gh_bin" issue close "$open" -R "$repo" --reason completed || exit 1
     echo "closed #$open"
   else
+    # Record the green commit on the last (closed) issue, so an older red run
+    # that finishes later does not open a new issue.
+    [ -z "$latest" ] || set_marker "$latest"
     echo "green, no open red issue"
   fi
   exit 0

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+## #3184 - Post-merge gate: one independent run per merge
+
+**Decided.** `post-merge.yml` uses one concurrency group for each commit,
+`post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, with `cancel-in-progress:
+false`. Each push runs on a free `camcraft-post-merge` runner and always
+finishes. The `gate` job does not change. The `report` job has its own
+group, `post-merge-report` (`cancel-in-progress: false`), and checks out the
+full history (`fetch-depth: 0`). `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh`
+keeps the last reported commit in a hidden marker in the rolling issue body,
+`<!-- post-merge-last-sha: <sha> -->`. A run whose commit is a strict
+ancestor of that commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, not the same
+commit) prints a notice and reports nothing.
+
+**Why.** With one group for `main`, a second push waited and a third push
+cancelled the waiting run. A red run then covered several merges, and the
+breaking merge needed a bisect (#3111). With one run for each commit, a red
+run names one commit. Runs can now finish out of order, so the report must
+not let an older green run close the issue of a newer red run.
+
+**Details chosen.**
+- The marker is read from the newest rolling issue, open or closed. A green
+  run with no open issue writes its commit into the closed issue's marker.
+  Without that, an older red run that finishes later would open a new issue
+  after a newer green run.
+- The same commit (a re-run) is not older than itself, and it reports.
+- If git cannot resolve the marker or this commit, the run reports as
+  before (fail open to a report, never to silence).
+- A new red issue carries the marker in its body. A red comment and a green
+  close write the marker into the issue body (the old marker line is
+  replaced).
+
+**Dropped.**
+- A repository variable or a separate state file for the last sha: the
+  issue asks for no new secrets or variables, and the rolling issue is
+  already the one shared state.
+- Comparing commit dates instead of ancestry: dates of merge commits are not
+  an order guarantee.
+
+**Known limit.** GitHub keeps at most one pending job in a concurrency
+group. If three report jobs wait at once, GitHub cancels the middle one.
+That report is lost; the next run on `main` reports the newer state. With
+two runners and a gate of about 20 min, three reports at once are rare.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Low. The marker is one line in the issue body;
+removing the guard returns the old behaviour.
